newsitem.title: PERU: Peru pledges peaceful solution despite provocation.
newsitem.headline: Peru pledges peaceful solution despite provocation.

text.p: Peru pledged on Saturday it would ensure a peaceful solution to the 39-day hostage crisis despite several days of provocative police manoeuvres intended to unnerve Marxist rebels holding 73 VIP hostages.
"We are going to take the time needed to reach a peaceful solution to this crisis without bloodshed," Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi said.

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) has accused the government of preparing for a storming of the besieged Japanese ambassador's home by staging military operations around the building in recent days.

Armoured vehicles have rolled up to the residence on two occasions, while a police helicopter has been flying overhead and troops have periodically taken up positions around the perimieter wall with guns trained on the building.

Pandolfi insisted, however, that the activities -- which had been interpreted as simulating an attack or testing how far the rebels could be pushed before reacting -- were only preparations for a negotiated end to the crisis.

"What the police are doing is impose more security in the zone," said Pandolfi. "Let's not forget that probably shortly there will be conversations (between the two sides) and probably also the freeing of hostages and the exit from the residence of the members of the self-styled MRTA."
"The people who come out will have to be well-protected, expecially the members of the MRTA, and that is the responsibility of the police," he said.
Pandolfi gave no evidence, however, that talks were imminent. They have stalled over the government's refusal to consider the MRTA's main demand for the release of some 400 jailed comrades.
Despite the government's hard line, President Alberto Fujimori has offered the rebels safe passage to a foreign country provided they lay down arms and release the hostages.
But the rebels insist they will remain in the residence as long as it takes to secure freedom for the prisoners.

The roughly 15 heavily armed rebels reacted defiantly on Saturday morning to the police activities, broadcasting through a megaphone Peru's national anthem, two of their own revolutionary songs and a tirade of slogans.
"Long live the resistance! Long live the MRTA!" said one of the slogans, according to witnesses. "The objective of this mission is freedom or death," said another.
An armoured personnel carrier approached the main entrance at 10:30 p.m. on Friday (0330 GMT Saturday) with special forces police on board training their rifles and machine guns on the residence.

Eight policemen, armed with assault rifles and night vision goggles, also rushed toward the compound's main entrance and crouched on either side training their guns on the building. Red laser beams were seen cutting across the garden to the house.

Another group of at least six police dressed in black combat gear crept in single file, pressed tight against the perimeter wall, as the armoured vehicle rumbled slowly along two sides of the compound before withdrawing from the area. One policeman was seen carrying a crossbow.

Earlier on Friday two personnel carriers passed right in front of the diplomatic compound twice and a helicopter flew overhead with an armed policeman in a harness riding on its skids. The helicopter returned on Saturday morning.
Although the police activities were the boldest yet, the rebels did not fire any warning shots as they have on several previous occasions since taking the compound on Dec. 17.

In a two-way radio conversation monitored by the local Radio Programas del Peru radio station, a man identifying himself as MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini said the activity had frightened the hostages but did not bother the rebels.
Fujimori met with his negotiator, Education Minister Domingo Palermo, on Saturday, and reiterated that he would not let the MRTA siege throw his government off track.
"We will not stop, nor will we change direction," he said. "Those who put stones in our way can be sure of that."
